title: What have you made and why did you make it?
author: BuffaloConscious7919
selftext:
There's so many individual posts of people making games but hardly anyone shares the story behind it.

  
Did it come from the dreams you had as a kid? Was it just a random experiment? Did you always want to make it?

  
Share you game and the reason you made it.

comments.author: Front-Pay3056

comments.author: NinjaLegacyDev
comments.body:
For years I was hoping that an old mobile game called “Ninja Royale” would eventually return. It never did. I listen to a ton of podcasts and one of them was talking about how people were remaking copies of games using ai vibe coding. I heard Claude was a great option for this so I downloaded Claude and just asked it how I would go about remaking the game with no experience of any kind. Around this same time I got really into another mobile game that someone had made by doing the same thing. Shortly after that, another person obtained the right to the original game and so that developer had to shut down their version. After hearing this, I knew that could happen to me one day so I took what Claude had developed so far and I started making it my own game. I have played a ton of games over my life and many of them had features that I really liked. I’ve implemented those good features into my game without just copying straight from those other games. I’ve also been brainstorming new ideas on how I can expand on the player experience so the game doesn’t start getting bogged down with too many systems. I did actually have a dream that ended up becoming an update that I loved after it got added. Where my game currently sits is around a month of providing ideas to Claude and using chatgpt to make my prompts more concise so I’m not overusing usage the way I was when I was running Claude on opus 5.5 while always using extra effort. The game is in early beta as I fill it out and create content to replace placeholders. It’s single player with coded bots so the players can still have a feel of what the game will be like once I have Claude code the back end systems that will allow me to connect it to Supabase for holding accounts and progress. Currently progress is stored on the players local device.

Now onto what the game is:

🥷🏼 Ninja Legacy

It’s a semi-multiplayer rpg where players can choose from 14 different ninja clans each with their own unique animal/creature they’re inspired by and each having their own element. The combat is turn based and is inspired by games like Avatar Fight HD and DOFUS. Your clan has unique combat skills (spells) such as single target or multi target attacks, buffs, debuffs, shields, healing, and passive skills that amplify certain aspects of combat. There are also currently 10 trainable skills such as Woodchopping, fishing, brewing, meditation, taming (this will be replaced with athletics), gearcraft, and more. The game has guilds where players can join and chat, PvP duels, quests (coming soon), a boss rush end game combat mode where you can earn your level 100-150 gear, 14 elemental towers that grant resources, gold, and gear, your own trophy case to show off your rare drops, a player market, a collection log that tracks your rare drops, leaderboards, and my favorite part…the Explore mode. Exploring is a mode you can play that is a screen to screen semi-open world that works a lot like dofus’ world setup. You can fight enemies, find and defeat multiple regional bosses for rare drops, locate Chests that contain gold, materials, gear, keys to rarer chests that contain powerful equipment (careful, some chests are mimics or might be boobytrapped), and you can even stumble across rare Asian mythological enemies like the Ekek and defeat it to earn a unique dagger with special effects. While exploring the world of currently 181 areas and multiple regions with enemies that fit their environment, you can also train your skilling, get tips from local villagers about where to locate certain resources, unlock teleports to fast travel, and enjoy finding every part of the map. You can switch clans anytime using a special potion so you won’t be paying to swap like some other games have. There will never be paying to win added into the game because I think everything should be earned and not purchased. Accomplishments should mean something when other players view your trophy case. I also forgot to mention there are achievements you can get which unlock player titles you can show off. There’s a pet system where you unlock pets by skilling or as a rare drop from bosses. There’s so much more to the game but I’m tired of typing so if you want to check it out, just know I do know it’s still kinda janky and I will clean up any jankiness you come across after I get all the content in the game.

You can play it on itch.io using the link below (I recommend Google Chrome so that your browser doesn’t wipe your cache after closing as you will lose your progress if that happens:

https://ninjalegacy.itch.io/ninja-legacy

Im really wanting to grow the official discord as well. This is where I post all game updates and really want some more feedback since im biased due to being the creator so I already know all the games systems and my brother has given feedback but I need more:

https://discord.gg/DN32KS4t35

comments.author: eschaff2114
comments.body: The ones that are coming out now are to hopefully give income so I can make Wistlings. It wasn’t something that I had always thought of or considered, but I played Spiritfarer in one of the hardest moments of my life and loved how it helped me through the grief. Wistlings takes a different spin on grief by looking at the things lost or left behind, but aren’t necessarily death. The person you loved who didn’t love you back, the family who rejected you, the grandparent that died when you were really young out of nowhere so you didn’t get to say goodbye. We go through so much and I think it will be nice to help people feel seen. The game will be based in an observatory and the main character helps the Wistling through their grief and completes tasks with them, and once they are ready to let go, helps them move on and become a constellation. The whole idea is caring and realizing you can grieve something and also let it go, but a part of it will always be there, it just doesn’t have to take up all the space in the room forever.

comments.author: hparamore
comments.body:
Anyone here ever played Banjo Kazooie? They do something really cool with the music where it is no playing a tune, but when you walk close to like a different world entrance, the music changes instruments in the style of that world. The tune and the tempo and everything is still the same, the instruments just fade.

I made an engine that takes music tracks I make, re-staffs them, and changes the instruments to fit a specific style. So it’s the same track, same tune, different instruments and feel.

And then in my game I have been working on, the other half of this tool fades the tracks between each style as the player scrolls between levels.

… and then I did that for all 8 tracks in my game, for all 10 different game modes lol. (A simple mobile matching game with like 80 tracks in it lol.)

I made a small part of it work on my website, so you can try it out. Scroll down.  
(And while you’re there, if you’re on iOS, go Download the test flight version, or “pre load” the game on the App Store. That would help me out a lot as I am getting ready to launch this next week!)

Link to website. Scroll down a bit.  
https://hexquest.app

comments.author: dpdmp-creation
comments.body:
Un jour j’ai eu l’idée d’un concept de jeu de société simple : Primary Color.  
Une grille, des couleurs primaires à combiner pour obtenir des couleurs secondaires et ternaires.   
J’ai codé moi-même le jeu en JS.   
Puis 7 ans plus tard, j’ai voulu regarder ce qu’était l’IA, par curiosité et attrait pour les nouveautés technologiques (geek ?).  
Et pour aller plus loin avec l’IA et passer le cap des prompts de type « dessine moi un vache qui souffle des bougies sur un gâteau rose » j’ai décidé de reprendre mon concept de jeu.  
Et 7 ans l’avoir créé je me suis aperçus qu’aucun jeu équivalent n’existait.  
Le premiers tests du jeu par des personnes de mon entourage ont été positifs, donc j’ai poursuivi le vibecoding avec une approche structuré et méthodique.  
Je suis développeur professionnel depuis 28 ans donc j’ai pu guider les IA de façon rigoureuse. Bien cadrer et définir en entrée, et toujours tester dans le détail.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/4annk0mu3m2i1.png

Back when I did games in BASIC (early 80s) there was a game that did a line of asterisks:

\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*              \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*              \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*              \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*             \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*       0       \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

The zero was a car, then it would add a new line at the top, and they'd all shift down. I wanted to do that but one line of pixels at a time.

So a conversation started. How can we do it more performatively? Can we pre-back this? What if we do it in layers and add this and that .... then it turned into the [game ](https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement)I have now.

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body:
I like cozy games and farming sims and I saw common complaints from folks in the genre about representation and customization.
There was a lot of me going "if I made a game like this i'd-" ideas.
The more I played games in the genre the more I saw what players talked about too. Lack of black hairstyles, no accessibility support, no options for prosthetics, NPCs that were bitter about being 'Stuck' in wheelchairs, wheelchairs in games that were just decor...
I think if you're playing a life sim you should have options for stuff that makes you feel connected to the character.
Thinking on that got me thinking on what a game could look like if you made it with that in mind from the start.
